alignments.note: One adjective rendered by the compound crook backed; head on crook, which carries the distinguishing lexeme by rule 31's subtraction, backed alone naming nothing.
Substantival adjective with the indefinite a, which belongs to the nominal expression under rule 15.

The noun stands in a nominal slot with no antecedent and no relative morpheme, so the that the ASV supplies to make the clause a noun phrase joins its unit under rule 46's headless-relative provision; head on the lexeme-bearing blemish, with the indefinite a going to the nominal expression under rule 15. The unit is discontinuous around the supplied hath, which is aligned separately: every other morpheme of the clause keeps its own English — be- takes in, the suffix takes his, 'ayin takes eye — so rule 43's subtraction finds nothing diminished by dropping the have but the possession the ASV supplied. Keeping hath inside this unit as part of the recasting was the competing reading.

The clause writes no hayah, no possessive preposition free to carry the word — the be- has its own in — no suffix without its own pronoun, and no verb the have renders, so nothing in it makes it possessive and the supplied hath answers to no morpheme (rules 43, 20, 30). Rule 43 forbids folding such a word into the noun or into a preposition standing elsewhere; the competing reading keeps it with tevallul.
Predicate noun with the construction-supplied copula (rule 20).
Noun rendered by the predicate adjective scabbed; the copula is written once for the coordinated predicates and shared under rules 22 and 34.

The construct adjective keeps the participle broken, which is its lexeme; the ASV's hath is the clause's supplied possessive frame and is aligned separately, since dropping it leaves this morpheme its whole rendering (rules 31, 43). The unit is discontinuous from its own object under rule 25.

meroach 'ashekh writes no hayah, no possessive preposition, no suffix and no verb the have renders — the same absence that leaves the supplied his added below — so the supplied hath is its own added unit under rule 43's closing case and rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause. Keeping it with meroach was the competing reading, rejected because that participle keeps broken when the word is dropped.

No suffix or other possessive morpheme stands on 'ashekh, so the supplied his answers to nothing in the source (rule 18's closing sentence, rule 30). Rule 15's ownership of a supplied determiner does not reach a supplied possessive.

review_notes: Corrected: the two supplied hath's are now their own added units. The accepted alignment marked the supplied his added on the ground that no possessive morpheme stands in the meroach 'ashekh clause, yet kept the supplied hath of that same clause with the participle; rule 43 puts both in the same position, since dropping the have leaves every written morpheme its own rendering and diminishes only the possession the English supplied.

The same subtraction governs tevallul be-'eyno: be- carries in, the suffix carries his, 'ayin carries eye and tevallul carries a blemish, so nothing is left for the hath to complete and it is added under rules 43 and 20.

The supplied that is kept with tevallul: rule 46 licenses the noun-phrase machinery the ASV must supply for a clause standing in a nominal slot with no antecedent and no 'asher, while rules 20 and 43 exclude a supplied lexical or possessive verb from that same frame. LEV.21.18's he that hath a flat nose is the contrasting case, where the whole phrase renders one participle and no other morpheme stands in the item.
The remaining units are unchanged: crook backed heads on crook, the copula of is scurvy is shared with scabbed under rule 22, and each 'o takes its own or.
